title: The Big Book of Casseroles: 250 Recipes for Serious Comfort Food

The Big Book of Casseroles boasts over 250 recipes (including low-fat and vegetarian dishes), plus handy planning, freezing, and storage tips. title: Forgotten Church Supper Recipes: Old-Fashioned Casseroles, Family Suppers, Potluck Favorit
description: Remember the casseroles, potluck dishes, and homemade desserts that everyone brought to church suppers? The tables were filled with bubbling casseroles, homemade rolls, creamy salads, baked beans, and cakes cut into generous squares. Neighbors exchanged recipes, families returned for seconds, and favorite dishes became part of the memories people carried home. Forgotten Church Supper Recipes , part of the Vintage Recipes Series, brings that style of American home cooking back to the kitchen with 60 old-fashioned recipes inspired by church potlucks, fellowship dinners, and community cookbook favorites. This collection combines recognizable comfort foods with less-common dishes that deserve another look. The emphasis is on familiar ingredients, practical preparation, satisfying family meals, and food meant to be shared. Inside you'll find: Old-Fashioned Casseroles: Chicken Spaghetti Casserole, Johnny Marzetti, Tater Tot Hotdish, Chicken Divan, and other covered-dish favorites. Hearty Family Suppers: Chicken and Dumplings, Porcupine Meatballs, Ham Loaf with Brown Sugar-Mustard Glaze, and Slow-Braised Pot Roast. Traditional Potluck Sides: Funeral Potatoes, Southern Pineapple Cheese Casserole, Baked Corn Pudding, and Molasses and Bacon Baked Beans. Retro Salads: Overnight Seven-Layer Salad, Copper Pennies, Three-Bean Salad, Ambrosia, and Lime Gelatin Salad. Homemade Breads: Refrigerator Yeast Rolls, Buttermilk Drop Biscuits, Southern Spoon Bread, and Skillet Cornbread. Old-Fashioned Desserts: Texas Chocolate Sheet Cake, Sour Cream Raisin Pie, Pineapple Upside-Down Cake, and Peach Cobbler. title: The Art of Homemade Casseroles: Noodles, Rice, Potatoes, Chicken, Beef, Vegetables, Creamy
description: Bring comfort, order, and real supper back to the table with The Art of Homemade Casseroles, a practical guide to one of the most dependable forms of home cooking. Casseroles have fed families, stretched ingredients, warmed church tables, rescued leftovers, and turned simple pantry staples into satisfying meals for generations. This book treats them with care—not as rushed mixtures thrown into a dish, but as thoughtful one-dish suppers with flavor, structure, moisture, contrast, and purpose. Inside, you will learn how to build casseroles that actually work: creamy without being heavy, hearty without being dry, economical without tasting plain, and comforting without becoming dull. The book explains how to balance foundations, main ingredients, vegetables, sauces, binders, seasonings, and toppings so every casserole feels complete when it reaches the table. Whether you are cooking for family, preparing meals ahead, using leftovers, stocking the freezer, or making a warm supper after a long day, this book gives clear guidance for real home kitchens. The recipes cover noodle and pasta casseroles, rice casseroles, potato bakes, chicken and turkey casseroles, beef casseroles, vegetable casseroles, breakfast casseroles, pork, ham, and sausage dishes, pantry and leftover casseroles, freezer-friendly meals, creamy bakes, tomato-based casseroles, hearty gratins, savory bread puddings, egg bakes, one-dish suppers, and comforting family meals built around everyday ingredients. You will find recipes using chicken, beef, turkey, ham, sausage, tuna, rice, noodles, potatoes, beans, vegetables, cheese, eggs, broths, gravies, cream sauces, tomato sauces, crumbs, crackers, herbs, and simple pantry staples. title: The Totally Not Boring Casserole Cookbook: Homemade Casserole Recipes That Save Your Walle
description: Get ready for a tasty trip through the world of casseroles! This cookbook is packed with easy-to-make recipes that'll have your family asking for seconds. From cheesy pasta bakes to hearty meat dishes, there's something for everyone. We've got all the classics you love, like chicken and rice casserole and tuna noodle bake. But we've also thrown in some surprises, like a zucchini and eggplant bake that'll make you forget you're eating veggies! And for those with a sweet tooth, don't worry - we've got breakfast casseroles that are practically dessert. What's great about these recipes is how simple they are. Most use ingredients you probably already have in your kitchen. And the best part? You can make them ahead of time, pop them in the fridge, and bake them when you're ready. It's perfect for busy families or anyone who wants a hot, homemade meal without spending hours in the kitchen. Each recipe comes with easy-to-follow instructions and handy tips to make your casserole even better. We've even included some vegetarian options, so there's truly something for everyone. Whether you're cooking for a big family dinner, a potluck with friends, or just want some tasty leftovers for the week, this cookbook has got you covered. These casseroles are comfort food at its best - warm, filling, and oh-so-satisfying. description: A good casserole is the easiest way to feed a family: one dish, one oven, and dinner that waits patiently until everyone is at the table. description: Take a stroll down memory lane with old-fashioned casserole recipes our mothers, grandmothers, and previous generations made in the days that are still amazing today! Casseroles have always been popular, especially when our mothers, grandmothers, and previous generations made them. And there are good reasons for it! They are perfect make-ahead meals that will save you time and money. You can also freeze them for later serving. It is also a choice dish for potluck parties. And most of all, they are delicious, very comforting, and satisfying. From the timeless and favorite casserole dishes like overnight breakfast casseroles to tuna noodle casseroles, scalloped potatoes, turkey tetrazzini, and more, you'll find over 90 vintage casserole dishes in this cookbook, along with tips and helpful information for making delicious casseroles. All you have to do is get the ingredients, spend a little time prepping, and pop the casserole in the oven!
